title: Reasoning effort and convergence: three OpenAI models
description: GPT-5.6 Luna, Terra, and Sol attempted the same interrupted-deployment repair under selected reasoning efforts, measuring the tradeoff between speed, cost, and durable convergence.
observations: GPT-5.6 Sol medium completed all three repairs at a 2:06 median, but had the highest known cost at $0.8162.
GPT-5.6 Terra medium was fastest at a 1:05 median and completed two of three repairs.
GPT-5.6 Luna completed two of three at high effort and one of three at medium effort; medium was faster (1:41 versus 2:03) and cheaper ($0.0845 versus $0.1022).
All four failures were classified as release-not-converged, so extra reasoning did not guarantee durable convergence on this incident.
notes: This is a controlled but small effort/convergence study: 12 total trials across one scenario and four model-effort lanes.
All matrices use the same Replaybook commit, scenario-pack version, host harness, Claux release, timeout, and three-attempt design.
Results are not a general ranking of the models or a universal recommendation for one reasoning level.
reproduction_command: python integrations/host/run_host_matrix.py --scenario-pack ../replaybook-infra --scenario 024-discourse-interrupted-deploy --models openai/gpt-5.6-luna --reasoning-efforts medium high --attempts 3 --concurrency 1 --base-port 30200; python integrations/host/run_host_matrix.py --scenario-pack ../replaybook-infra --scenario 024-discourse-interrupted-deploy --models openai/gpt-5.6-terra openai/gpt-5.6-sol --reasoning-efforts medium --attempts 3 --concurrency 1 --base-port 30100
